conviction_note: Pinewood is in the last days of a recommended 448p cash scheme (Ridgeview/U.K. Piston Bidco). Shareholders approved it 99.76% on 25 Sep, the court hearing is 7 Oct, last dealings are 8 Oct, and spot at 446.2p sits 0.4% under the offer. The interims cannot move a pinned price outside a tail I could not source (a MAC-style break or a rival bid), so both the sum and the expected move are 0.

already_public.what: Rule 2.7 firm recommended cash offer of 448p per share (about £545m), with irrevocables around 48.68% at announcement; this caps the price and makes the H1 numbers irrelevant to value
Court Meeting (99.76% of scheme shares voted in favour) and General Meeting passed; court hearing expected 7 Oct, last day of dealings 8 Oct, Effective 9 Oct, delisting by 12 Oct
Notice of Interim Results: H1 to 30 Jun 2026 on Wed 30 Sep, analyst presentation 09:00 BST

new_in_release.expect: the H1 2026 numbers are unknown; they are irrelevant to price because the 448p cash offer is shareholder-approved and awaits only court sanction
unlikely to carry a meaningful outlook given the take-private; irrelevant to price either way
a declared interim dividend could reduce the offer price by the same amount under the 2.7 terms (Bidco's reserved right), which is price-neutral to holders; no sign one is coming
the only price-relevant lines would be scheme-timetable or conditions news; none is expected in the interims

bar: unsourced for the H1 numbers (one analyst, Yahoo empty). The relevant bar is the 448p cash offer, https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/pinewood-technologies-group--pine/replacement-recommended-acquisition-of-pinewood-/9730381. Sizes capped at 0.

positioning_check: FCA aggregated register: 4.88% net short at 2026-09-22 (baseline, https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv), down from 5.17%, so covering. In a cash scheme priced 0.4% below a shareholder-approved offer, these shorts are probably hedges or legacy positions and not directional fuel. A squeeze is capped by the offer unless a rival bidder appears, so the baseline's short_squeeze lean component (+2.93) does not apply to this name.

baseline_tension: The evidence cuts against the baseline lean. Its +3.56 comes almost entirely from the short-squeeze component, which cannot operate on a stock pinned 0.4% below a shareholder-approved cash offer. The 60-day run-up of +48.7% is the bid premium, not momentum. So the expected move is 0 rather than anything toward the lean.
language_note: Nothing the English sources did not already carry. The RNS record on Investegate (the scheme, the court and general meeting results, the Feoh letter-of-intent sell-down) carries the same facts the English wire copy summarises. For a name in a live offer period, the domestic RNS channel is the primary source, and it is also exactly what the wires read.
lessons_applied: nothing changed. 'In a live bid, results are noise; the offer is the finding' agrees with the draft, and the offer is already priced (0.4% spread), so it adds no sized finding. The 'understatement' and '3-7% base' rules were considered and not applied, because the move is capped by a court-pending cash offer and not by the reaction distribution.
